instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Can You Keep It?
cards.instruction: Use increasingly sensitive details to test whether someone deserves deeper trust.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club menu changes next month. Keep that out of the committee chat; I'm checking who I can brief.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll just tell Sam. He helps me with the ordering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No forwarding through useful people. The chef has resigned. Can you keep that out of an order form?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order the usual quantities. Nobody needs a reason from me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I accepted her resignation because I'm taking over the kitchen. Please let me tell Sam that myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I withdrew my college application. Have you told Mum?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No. I told her you were still deciding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't replace my silence with a plan I haven't made. I've leased a bakery. Can I send you the address?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Call me. Mum uses my tablet; she'd see the message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Take the call somewhere you can stay alone. It's Mum's old bakery.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Hand Over the Proof
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the note about cancelling my exhibition space. I need to see what the curator actually wrote.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says, 'You can't exhibit unless the committee agrees.' They won't.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Her words finish at 'agrees'? Your prediction isn't part of the note. Hand me the page, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's personal stuff about me on the page. I'm not handing that over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fold your part underneath and let me read the condition. We can discuss your forecast afterwards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't sign the club accounts from a number you read out. Give me the receipt-drawer key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've added it twice. Both totals match.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Adding the same omissions twice produces very tidy agreement. We'll check receipt by receipt. The key, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If there's a mistake, the committee will put it on me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we correct it here, together. Start by unlocking the drawer; you can explain each receipt while I check.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That ink on your new sofa must be from the delivery label. Leave it alone while we establish the source.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The label's dry. You signed with your fountain pen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then test the signature, not the label. The driver may have brushed it against the sofa. Photograph the contact point.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your pen is still leaking onto the cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lift it by the clip, please. The delivery must have cracked it squeezing past me. Get the damaged pen in the same photograph.

cards.title: Anything but That Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every attempt to discuss the one detail that could expose your real motive or involvement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give you the spare key over dinner. Have you booked a table?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I never gave you a spare. Where did it come from?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One arrangement at a time, please. We need a confirmed table before we discuss what happens over it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's confirmed for two. Did my sister give you the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If we're including your sister, we need three places. Ring the restaurant before you invite anyone else.

cards.title: A Kinder Version
cards.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The gallery says your portrait needs a stronger likeness. Let's take that as a practical note.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They didn't recognize you, did they?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Recognition depends on more than a face. Use the shirt I wore for the sitting as a reference; they need a clear identifying feature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I painted the shirt exactly. They asked why I'd put it on somebody else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the shirt is working. We'll bring the face into line with it. Start with the jaw; leave the part they recognized alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nina's dinner is just a small group. Let's make another plan; I'll book us noodles.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's invited the whole choir. Read me the message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We don't need to read an invitation like a rejection letter. She wants an uncomplicated evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm in that choir. Does the message say I'm complicated?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, I'm not reading that bit aloud. We're dealing with one dinner, not grading your whole personality. Let me book somewhere we'll both enjoy.
